Deductions: the two source-migration change ids printed on the fragment table have no durable log in the run directory, so a later reader cannot open their provenance; and the two reviewed commits are local-only by the worker non-push rule, which is expected but leaves the record unlanded until a merge.
justifications.evidence: The evidence is primary and separates the two states: gap-read-pre.log carries the negative arm of the split's own assertion (negative_control.ok=false with the three measurement sources reported on gap_at_outboard_midplane and revived_name_is_live false), and gap-after.log carries the positive arm (after_state_assertion.ok=true). A readback that could not separate the states would pass both, so this one is discriminating. Preview and apply receipts carry a sha256 chain (manifest_sha256=e70e4ceb..., authority_file_sha256 eda4cad7...). Deductions: the change-id table's two source-migration ids are not durably logged in the run directory, and the manifest's negative_control_log is description-shaped.
justifications.fit: The node followed the repository's own conventions throughout: it reused the signed-repair envelope (build_repair_authority + apply_signed_manifest) instead of hand-writing the revive, reused the deterministic source mover (retarget_standard_name_sources) instead of editing PRODUCED_NAME by hand, followed the evidence-fragment layout with node-id-prefixed element ids and a project-absolute figure src, and drew the figure to the repository's data-ink rules (direct labels, one feature hue for the moved sources, grey for the kept one, no gridlines).
justifications.goal_fidelity: The dispatched goal -- move the three midplane measurement distances off gap_at_outboard_midplane onto a revived radial_separatrix_distance_at_outboard_midplane -- is achieved exactly and in the direction asked. gap-after.log shows the three sources on the revived name and the separatrix source alone on the holder, and the revived name at name_stage drafted / status draft / superseded_from_stage removed, which is live. The first pass was blocked and the node took the coordinator-authorised signed route rather than forcing the fold owner, which the fragment route section records honestly (the two revive_previews in gap-read-pre.log both return ok=false with the reason stated).
justifications.reuse: Searched imas_codex/standard_names and imas_codex/graph for an existing owner of the family-state readback before scoring this. Every writer definition delegates to an owner (retarget_standard_name_sources provenance_lifecycle.py:505; apply_signed_manifest signed_manifest.py:7582; build_repair_authority repair_authority.py:135; supersede_into edit.py:2886 for the refused preview) and re-implements nothing. The bespoke readback helpers (read_names, read_source_bindings, writer_quiescence, after_state_assertion) have no library owner: the nearest, edit.py:1875 _bound_source_ids, returns source ids bound to one name and projects neither name_stage nor the produced_sn_id scalar mirror, and the graph_ops/attachment_audit PRODUCED_NAME readers likewise do not. No owner exists, so no score penalty is owed; the deduction reflects that the readback lives only in the one-shot fragment rather than extending a shared reader.
justifications.scope_discipline: Three of four changed paths are inside the dispatched write paths, and the graph mutations are confined to the four-family names the node was chartered to touch with the writer owners used as sentinels. The single out-of-scope path (shc-gap-family-split-manifest.json) is the one the coordinator authorised after the dispatch was cut, and the node disclosed it rather than widening its own declaration to silence the check -- which is the correct handling of a scope change, but it is still a path written outside the original fence and check-manifest consequently exits 1.
